title: BabelJudge: Measuring LLM-as-a-Judge Reliability Across Languages and Agent Trajectories
what_it_does: Framework measuring judge position bias, verbosity bias, order inconsistency, and cross-lingual degradation across English, Hindi, Arabic, Swahili via controlled perturbations.
key_results: Documents judge reliability degradation across languages including Hindi.
drawbacks: Hindi appears in native Devanagari only.
gap_vs_ours: No script/transliteration condition at all; language, not script, is the variable.

title: Indi-RomCoM: Code-Mixed Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Romanized Indic-English Instructions
what_it_does: Benchmarks LLMs on romanized code-mixed Indic-English instructions across 7 tasks and 4 Indic languages with controlled code-mixing density.
key_results: LLMs consistently underperform on romanized code-mixed instructions, degrading with code-mixing density.
drawbacks: Task-performance benchmark; instructions vary rather than holding content fixed.
gap_vs_ours: No judge-scoring bias; no native-script twin condition for a judge to score.

title: Lower-Resource, Higher Scores: Language Bias in LLM Evaluators
what_it_does: Audits multilingual LLM evaluators on semantically identical instruction-response pairs across 23 languages, measuring language-dependent score shifts.
key_results: Systematic cross-model score shifts, up to 43% acceptance-rate difference across languages; lower-resource languages scored MORE favorably; language identity predictive even after controlling for uncertainty.
drawbacks: Compares across languages in standard scripts only; translation-based pairs introduce noise.
gap_vs_ours: Closest methodological neighbour, but varies language rather than writing system; confirms the language axis can run OPPOSITE to expectations, motivating our script-only isolation.

title: One Language, Two Scripts: Probing Script-Invariance in LLM Concept Representations
what_it_does: Uses Serbian Cyrillic/Latin digraphia to probe whether LLM internal concept representations are script-invariant.
key_results: Finds imperfect cross-script transfer: script non-invariance exists inside models.
drawbacks: Interpretability probing only; Serbian, not Devanagari/romanized Indic.
gap_vs_ours: The exact same-language-two-scripts control paradigm, but at representation level with no judge-scoring outcome.

title: Script Sensitivity: Benchmarking Language Models on Unicode, Romanized and Mixed-Script Sinhala
what_it_does: Benchmarks 24 open LMs on native Unicode vs romanized vs mixed-script Sinhala with language fixed.
key_results: Over 300x median perplexity degradation from native Unicode to romanized Sinhala; single-script evaluation underestimates deployment risk.
drawbacks: Perplexity/LM-quality only; not Devanagari/Hindi.
gap_vs_ours: Script duality with language fixed, but no LLM-as-judge and no content-quality scoring; supports the mechanism behind our hypothesis.

title: The Tokenizer Tax: Quantifying and Explaining the Cross-Lingual Cost of Subword Tokenization for Indian Languages
what_it_does: Quantifies the token premium of English-centric subword tokenizers on Indian languages; attributes it mechanistically to failed BPE merges leaving Indic text in single-byte fallback tokens.
key_results: Indian languages pay average 8.0x tokenization tax vs English (up to 13.0x Malayalam); effective context shrinks to ~12%; merge-failure rate correlates with the tax at r=0.89; multilingual tokenizers cut the tax ~73%.
drawbacks: Single-author preprint, not peer-reviewed; stops at token counts and merge statistics without behavioral experiments.
gap_vs_ours: Provides the precise byte-fallback fragmentation mechanism we hypothesize but never tests its behavioral consequence on judge scores.

title: Toward Robust LLM-Based Judges: Taxonomic Bias Evaluation and Debiasing Optimization (JudgeBiasBench)
what_it_does: Taxonomy of 12 LLM-judge bias types across 4 dimensions with bias-augmented instances and RL/contrastive debiasing.
key_results: State-of-the-art catalog of judge biases.
drawbacks: Script/orthography/romanization is not among the taxonomized bias types.
gap_vs_ours: Direct evidence the community has not yet named script bias in judges; our paper fills the missing taxonomy slot.

title: Towards Reliable Multilingual LLMs-as-a-Judge: An Empirical Study
what_it_does: Empirical study of building multilingual LLM judges (English/Spanish/Basque): instruction translation, mono vs multilingual supervision, model size.
key_results: Characterizes low-resource judge weaknesses and supervision strategies.
drawbacks: All three languages are Latin-script; no Indic languages.
gap_vs_ours: No script, transliteration, or romanization dimension.

title: COMI-LINGUA: Expert Annotated Large-Scale Dataset for Multitask NLP in Hindi-English Code-Mixing
what_it_does: 125K+ instance triple-annotated Hindi-English code-mixed dataset covering five NLP tasks in both Devanagari and Roman script variants; benchmarks LLMs on it.
key_results: Closed-source LLMs beat traditional tools zero-shot; fine-tuning reaches up to 95.25 F1 on NER, 98.77 F1 on matrix-language ID.
drawbacks: Evaluates LLMs as task performers on code-mixed data; Hindi-English only.
gap_vs_ours: Shows LLMs can process Hinglish in both scripts for NLP tasks but never tests whether a judge rates identical content differently by script.

title: CodeMixBench: Evaluating Code-Mixing Capabilities of LLMs Across 18 Languages
what_it_does: Code-mixing benchmark of eight tasks across 18 languages in seven families, with a synthetic data pipeline (word substitution + GPT-4 prompting).
key_results: LLMs consistently underperform on code-mixed data, especially across language families; data, scale, and few-shot prompting partially close the gap.
drawbacks: Relies on synthetic code-mixed text that may not reflect natural Hinglish spelling variability.
gap_vs_ours: Measures LLM competence at handling code-mixed input, not the fairness of an LLM grader when the same answer appears code-mixed/romanized vs native.

title: How Reliable is Multilingual LLM-as-a-Judge?
what_it_does: Measures cross-lingual judgment consistency of five judge models across five tasks and 25 languages; proposes an ensemble strategy.
key_results: Only ~0.3 average Fleiss' Kappa consistency across languages, worst in low-resource languages; neither more multilingual data nor scale fixes it.
drawbacks: Consistency defined across translations between languages, conflating translation quality with judge behavior.
gap_vs_ours: Cannot attribute inconsistency to orthography because language and script co-vary; our transliteration design isolates script.

title: MorphTok: Morphologically Grounded Tokenization for Indian Languages
what_it_does: Morphology-aware pre-segmentation plus Constrained BPE handling Devanagari dependent vowel signs (matras) that standard BPE splits into meaningless tokens.
key_results: 1.68% fertility reduction for Indic scripts with comparable downstream performance; introduces EvalTok, a human-centric tokenization quality metric.
drawbacks: Modest improvements at small scale; requires retraining tokenizers.
gap_vs_ours: Documents exactly how Devanagari is mis-segmented by BPE but never traces mis-segmentation to evaluative behavior.

title: RomanLens: The Role Of Latent Romanization In Multilinguality In LLMs
what_it_does: Mechanistic interpretability (logit lens, activation patching) showing LLMs processing non-Roman-script languages represent target words in romanized form in intermediate layers.
key_results: Semantic concepts encoded similarly across native and romanized representations; romanization acts as a latent bridge for cross-lingual transfer.
drawbacks: Internal-representation findings do not quantify behavioral output differences from script choice.
gap_vs_ours: Explains why scripts may be processed asymmetrically inside the model but not whether that surfaces as score differences when the LLM judges.

title: Script Gap: Evaluating LLM Triage on Indian Languages in Native vs Romanized Scripts in a Real World Setting
what_it_does: Benchmarks LLMs on real user maternal-health triage queries in 5 Indian languages plus Nepali, comparing classification reliability on native vs romanized versions of the same messages.
key_results: Consistent degradation on romanized input, gaps up to 24 points across languages and models; projects ~2M excess triage errors at the partner org; proposes uncertainty-based selective routing.
drawbacks: Single classification task in one deployment context; may not generalize to open-ended generation or subjective quality assessment.
gap_vs_ours: Closest prior work; measures the LLM's own task accuracy on romanized input, not bias in an LLM-as-judge's scoring of content quality across scripts.

title: Airavata: Introducing Hindi Instruction-tuned LLM
what_it_does: Hindi instruction-tuned LLM (fine-tuned OpenHathi on IndicInstruct) with Hindi evaluation benchmarks including GPT-4-judged generation quality.
key_results: Outperforms base OpenHathi on most Hindi NLU/NLG tasks, demonstrating the value of Hindi instruction tuning.
drawbacks: LLM-judged evaluation adopted uncritically, without validating the judge against human raters.
gap_vs_ours: Evaluates Hindi in Devanagari only; never asks whether the GPT-4 judge would score the same content differently if romanized. Exemplifies the practice our study audits.

title: Breaking the Script Barrier in Multilingual Pre-Trained Language Models with Transliteration-Based Post-Training Alignment
what_it_does: Transliteration-based post-pretraining alignment mapping different writing systems into Latin script to improve cross-lingual transfer between related languages.
key_results: Up to 50% improvement on some downstream tasks in English-centric transfer; larger gains from non-English sources.
drawbacks: Targets encoder-style multilingual PLMs, not instruction-tuned generative LLMs used in evaluation pipelines.
gap_vs_ours: Treats script mismatch as a transfer obstacle to fix via training; does not consider script as a bias source in judge scoring.

title: IndicGenBench: A Multilingual Benchmark to Evaluate Generation Capabilities of LLMs on Indic Languages
what_it_does: Human-curated multi-way parallel generation benchmark (summarization, MT, QA) over 29 Indic languages spanning 13 scripts.
key_results: Every Indic language shows a significant gap vs English; lower-resource languages degrade most.
drawbacks: Automatic reference-based metrics rather than LLM/human judges; each language tested only in its conventional script.
gap_vs_ours: Covers 13 native scripts but never the same language in two scripts, so romanized-vs-native judge bias is untestable on it.

title: Justice or Prejudice? Quantifying Biases in LLM-as-a-Judge
what_it_does: CALM: automated perturbation-based framework quantifying a taxonomy of 12 biases in LLM judges (position, verbosity, self-enhancement, authority, bandwagon, etc.).
key_results: Even advanced judges that look robust in aggregate show significant persistent biases on specific tasks; judge reliability is task-dependent.
drawbacks: The 12-bias taxonomy is built and measured on English data only; perturbations never vary language or orthography.
gap_vs_ours: Script/transliteration bias is absent from the taxonomy; our study adds an orthography-level bias axis.

title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
what_it_does: Isolates self-preference bias: judges (GPT-4, Llama 2) recognize their own outputs and inflate scores for them.
key_results: Linear correlation between self-recognition accuracy and self-preference strength; fine-tuning that increases self-recognition also increases self-preference (causal link).
drawbacks: Only self-preference, English summarization-style tasks.
gap_vs_ours: Shows judges favor familiar-looking text (their own style) but never tests familiarity at the writing-system level.

title: METAL: Towards Multilingual Meta-Evaluation
what_it_does: Meta-evaluation dataset of 1,000 summaries across 10 languages with native-speaker judgments on 5 dimensions; measures LLM-judge/human agreement.
key_results: GPT-4 judges agree best with native speakers; GPT-3.5-Turbo poor; LLM evaluators' stated reasoning often mismatches human judges' reasoning.
drawbacks: Small per-language sample (100/language), single task (summarization).
gap_vs_ours: Judge-human agreement per language in standard script only; script-controlled judge sensitivity unexamined.

title: MILU: A Multi-task Indic Language Understanding Benchmark
what_it_does: India-centric multiple-choice benchmark, ~85K questions, 8 domains, 41 subjects, 11 Indic languages from regional exams.
key_results: Best model (GPT-4o) reaches only 74% average; language-specific fine-tuned models barely above random; drops on low-resource languages and cultural domains.
drawbacks: Multiple-choice accuracy sidesteps generation evaluation and judge reliability entirely.
gap_vs_ours: Native-script only, exact-match scored; no lever to detect script-driven bias in model-based scoring.

title: MM-Eval: A Multilingual Meta-Evaluation Benchmark for LLM-as-a-Judge and Reward Models
what_it_does: Multilingual meta-evaluation benchmark: 5 core subsets, 18 languages, plus a 122-language consistency subset stress-testing judges and reward models.
key_results: Evaluators strong in English are unfair and inconsistent on lower-resourced languages, tending to assign middling scores.
drawbacks: Measures per-language judge accuracy; does not manipulate orthographic form within a language.
gap_vs_ours: Its language-consistency axis stops at the language level; we extend consistency testing within one language to the script level.

title: MYTE: Morphology-Driven Byte Encoding for Better and Fairer Multilingual Language Modeling
what_it_does: Morpheme-based replacement for UTF-8 byte encoding so equivalent information yields comparably sized segments across languages, targeting the byte-fallback penalty on non-Latin scripts.
key_results: Shorter encodings than UTF-8 for all 99 languages studied (up to ~70% for Burmese); largest improvements for non-Latin scripts; reduced cross-lingual perplexity gaps.
drawbacks: Requires morphological resources and retraining; cannot diagnose or fix bias in existing deployed judges.
gap_vs_ours: Fixes byte-level segmentation inequity for scripts like Devanagari but never measures whether that inequity biases an existing LLM's quality judgments.

title: PARIKSHA: A Large-Scale Investigation of Human-LLM Evaluator Agreement on Multilingual and Multi-Cultural Data
what_it_does: Compares ~90K human evaluations with 30K LLM-judge evaluations of 30 models across 10 Indic languages, pairwise and direct assessment.
key_results: Human-LLM agreement fair for pairwise but drops sharply for direct assessment, worst for Bengali and Odia; GPT-based evaluator shows self-bias.
drawbacks: Analyzes agreement per language as-is without controlled manipulation of any single factor.
gap_vs_ours: Script is a confound rather than a treatment; we hold Hindi content constant and vary only Devanagari vs Latin.

title: RomanSetu: Efficiently unlocking multilingual capabilities of Large Language Models via Romanization
what_it_does: Uses romanized text as the interface for extending English-centric LLMs to non-Roman-script languages via continual pretraining and instruction tuning on romanized Indic data.
key_results: Romanization reduces token fertility 2x-4x vs native script and matches or outperforms native-script representation on NLU/NLG/MT; romanized embeddings align more closely with English.
drawbacks: Requires continual pretraining (not applicable to closed judges off-the-shelf); evaluates task accuracy on clean machine-transliterated text, not noisy user romanization.
gap_vs_ours: Studies romanization as an input strategy for task performance; never asks whether an LLM evaluator assigns different quality scores to identical content in romanized vs native script.

title: Tokenizer Choice For LLM Training: Negligible or Crucial?
what_it_does: Trains 24 LLMs (2.6B) ablating tokenizer algorithm, vocabulary size, and data to isolate the causal effect of tokenizer choice on downstream performance.
key_results: Tokenizer choice significantly affects performance and cost; English-centric tokenizers on multilingual data add up to 68% training cost; fertility metrics not reliably predictive of downstream performance.
drawbacks: Pretraining-scale effects on generation/understanding benchmarks, not frozen commercial judges or evaluation behavior.
gap_vs_ours: Shows tokenization affects what a model can do, not what it thinks of others' outputs; no fertility-to-judge-bias link.

title: Aksharantar: Open Indic-language Transliteration datasets and models for the Next Billion Users
what_it_does: Largest public transliteration dataset for Indian languages (26M pairs, 21 languages, 12 scripts) plus the IndicXlit transliteration model.
key_results: IndicXlit improves transliteration accuracy 15% over baselines on Dakshina; first public baselines for 7 languages.
drawbacks: Resource/model paper for the transliteration task itself, not a study of downstream LLM behavior.
gap_vs_ours: Supplies tooling to build our paired stimuli but contains no analysis of judge bias across scripts.

title: Are Large Language Model-based Evaluators the Solution to Scaling Up Multilingual Evaluation?
what_it_does: First large calibration study of GPT-4 as multilingual evaluator vs 20K human judgments across 3 tasks, 5 metrics, 8 languages including non-Latin scripts.
key_results: GPT-4 evaluators show systematic bias toward higher scores and poor calibration with native-speaker judgments, worst for lower-resource languages.
drawbacks: Each language evaluated only in its standard native orthography; one judge model.
gap_vs_ours: Includes Hindi in native script but never presents the same content in alternate scripts, so it cannot separate language bias from script bias.

title: Do All Languages Cost the Same? Tokenization in the Era of Commercial Language Models
what_it_does: Analyzes cost and utility of OpenAI's API across 22 languages, linking token-count variance to pricing fairness ('language taxes').
key_results: Speakers of many languages are simultaneously overcharged and receive poorer task results; affected populations live where pricing is least affordable.
drawbacks: Utility measured on task accuracy of the model as performer, not evaluator; no within-language script variation.
gap_vs_ours: Shows tokenization drives cost/performance inequity but never asks whether a judge scores the more expensively tokenized form of identical content lower.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
what_it_does: Formalizes the LLM-as-a-judge paradigm with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, validating LLM judges against human preferences and cataloguing judge failure modes (position, verbosity, self-enhancement bias).
key_results: GPT-4 judge matches human preferences with over 80% agreement (human-human level) while systematically exhibiting position and verbosity biases.
drawbacks: Almost entirely English-centric; bias analysis limited to a few coarse categories without linguistic dimensions.
gap_vs_ours: Does not examine language, script, or transliteration effects at all; we test whether identical content in Devanagari vs romanized Hindi receives different scores.

title: Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages
what_it_does: Measures cross-lingual tokenization length disparity ('token premium') for the same content across languages; inequity arises at the tokenization stage.
key_results: Same-content tokenization length differs up to 15x across languages; even byte/char-level models show over 4x differences, driving unequal cost, latency, and effective context.
drawbacks: Measures cost/length only; does not test whether longer tokenizations change model outputs or quality judgments.
gap_vs_ours: Establishes the token premium but never connects it to evaluation outcomes; no judge setting, no within-language script manipulation.

title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
what_it_does: Shows pairwise LLM evaluation is systematically vulnerable to positional bias (rankings hackable by reordering candidates); proposes a calibration framework.
key_results: Exploiting position alone makes Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT on 66 of 80 queries; calibration substantially improves alignment with humans.
drawbacks: Single bias type (position), English-only, small query set.
gap_vs_ours: Treats fairness as ordering robustness, not surface-form robustness; never asks whether the writing system of identical content shifts judge scores.

title: MEGA: Multilingual Evaluation of Generative AI
what_it_does: First comprehensive multilingual benchmarking of generative LLMs on 16 datasets across 70 languages vs SOTA fine-tuned models.
key_results: Generative LLMs lag substantially on many non-English (especially low-resource, non-Latin-script) languages; extended later by MEGAVERSE.
drawbacks: Classic reference-based metrics over standard tasks; measures task accuracy, not reliability of evaluation methods.
gap_vs_ours: Benchmarks capability per language but never controls script or examines judge scoring across scripts.

title: Romanization-based Large-scale Adaptation of Multilingual Language Models
what_it_does: Systematic study of UROMAN transliteration as a large-scale adaptation strategy for multilingual PLMs on 14 low-resource languages.
key_results: UROMAN-based transliteration strong for many languages; largest gains on unseen scripts and low-data setups.
drawbacks: mBERT/XLM-R-era models on classification tasks; UROMAN output differs from real user romanization (Hinglish spelling variation).
gap_vs_ours: Frames romanization as a capability booster for adaptation; no analysis of evaluation-time scoring fairness across scripts.

title: XLM-V: Overcoming the Vocabulary Bottleneck in Multilingual Masked Language Models
what_it_does: Scales a multilingual vocabulary to 1M tokens with per-language capacity allocation, addressing under-allocation for low-resource scripts.
key_results: Outperforms XLM-R on every tested task, up to 11.2% absolute on MasakhaNER; shorter, more meaningful tokenizations.
drawbacks: Encoder-only masked LM; vocabulary remedy does not transfer to fixed tokenizers of deployed generative judges.
gap_vs_ours: Shows vocabulary allocation drives representation quality for low-resource scripts; the link between vocabulary starvation and judge score deflation remains untested.
